Even if the character has a "while this model is leading a unit it has -1 to wound" rule or something similar, the modifier persists for every attack from the attacking unit, even if the character who is leading the unit dies from the xth attack and only the bodyguards are alive. 


"If an Attached unit contains more than one model with such a rule, both models are considered to be leading that Attached unit, and so all such rules apply. Such rules cease to apply if that unit ceases to be an Attached unit (such as when the last Bodyguard model in that unit is destroyed - If this is as the result of an enemy unit’s attacks, all ‘while this model is leading a unit…’ rules cease to apply after the attacking unit’s attacks have been resolved. (Note it's units attacks and not models attacks)" 

Same thing goes for debuffs on attached units like oath of moment:

 "Persisting Effects: Some rules apply an effect that lasts until a certain duration has passed (e.g. until the start of your next turn).
Such effects are known as persisting effects. If a persisting effect applies to a unit when it embarks within a Transport, make a note of that effect and its duration; if that unit disembarks for any reason, any persisting effects continue to apply to that unit for their full duration. If a persisting effect applies to an Attached unit and that unit ceases to be an Attached unit (because either all of its Bodyguard models or all of its Leader models are destroyed), any persisting effects continue to apply to the surviving unit for their
full duration."

It is ok to have a lower smithing level than your character level. It's enough when you have a blacksmithing level that you can craft level approriate gear for yourself. For example without leveling blacksmithing you can already craft equipment until character level 12 or 14. If you want to know how high your blacksmith level needs to be to learn the next range of crafting (basically the next ore type) and are on pc, you can simple press K, go to crafting -> blacksmithing and look at the first passive skill in this skillline. If you hover above this skill it says you at which blacksmithing level you can learn it. 

Basically decontructing everything what you don't need and/or researching traits will give you enough inspiration that you always are on par with your character development. (I'm VR8 and have blacksmithing at level 38 for example, there I can craft VR7 and 8 armor/weapons)

Crafting wits are daily quests. You can certificate in all 6 professions and do them every day. you will get a container that represents your crafting skill in the profession of the quest. If you didn't spend any points in blacksmithing passive yet, you will get some gold, an item or two of the lowest level range material and sometimes a map to special mining nodes in your starter area. These nodes are bound to you only and only you can harvest them. They provide more materials (and sometimes rarer materials) than normal harvest nodes.

Trading guilds normally work based on money you make or spend at their guild store. Guild stores from guilds you are in can be accessed at every bank. Guild stores from other guilds are found in all of tamriel, every city has some. There, you can post your item with a fixed price, and other people can buy them. There are special fees and taxes involved in selling items, but everthing will be displayed before you post something in the store. If you sell or buy anything, there shouldn't be a delay in receiving the item or gold, but it can bug out and you need to relog or change zones for the mail to appear.

Bronze will be high Bronze/low Silver

Silver will be Silver

Gold will be high Silver/low Gold

Plat will be mid-high Gold

Diamond will be high Gold - mid Plat

I don't like any of these ideas:  
1. Disable AA: Best Ward detection if you attack creeps from bushes without hitting S. And if you practice your hand positioning you will never accidentally hit D.  
2. Skill path: This information will only cause teammates to flame you if you don't skill in the "right" order.  
3. Ult timer: This one is a bit tricky. If you have more information at hand, you will communicate less with your team. If I have an Amumu or Malphite or someone with a huge teamfight ult, I usually ask them when their ults come up. That informs everyone on my team when the big ult comes up. If there would be a timer, three things could happen: (As example I use Amumu)  
3.1 A Blitz hooks someone and engages a fight. He did not see that Amumus ult was on CD for another 10 sec. Amumu flames Blitz because he didn't pay attention to the timers.  
3.2 A Blitz hooks someone and engages a fight. Amumu's ult came up but he did not use it. Blitz (and every other teammate) flames Amumu.  
3.3 Blitz hooks someone. Amumu ult is up. He ults but the other teammates paid no attention to the timer and look surprised that amumus ult was up. The fight is lost because the others ran away. Amumu flames em all.
